version.changelog: v2.1: enriched docs, why null-skill calibration, expanded triggers, README

llm.summary: This is a plausible skill and test-suite generator, but it under-documents how untrusted specs become agent instructions and claims safeguards the code does not implement.

dimensions.detail: Reading SKILL.md/spec files and writing generated SKILL.md/task_suite.yaml files fits the stated purpose, but optional --evaluate and --auto-improve invoke local tools from ~/.claude and can affect generated skill artifacts.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No postinstall script, dependency install hook, remote payload retrieval, or automatic execution mechanism was found; the behavior is exposed through manual Python CLI commands.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The --from-spec path copies user-supplied specification content into generated SKILL.md instructions, including an undocumented critical_constraints field that is rendered as forceful MUST instructions with little validation.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No background service, scheduler, credential access, or privilege escalation was found; persistence is limited to generated output files and optional in-place SKILL.md improvement when the user selects that mode.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core purpose is coherent, but artifact-backed mismatches exist: documentation claims null-skill calibration, PytestJudge generation, harness-pattern tasks, and atomic writes, while the inspected implementation does not perform those behaviors.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review generated SKILL.md files before installing them, especially when the spec comes from another person or includes critical constraints. Use private output directories, be cautious with --auto-improve because it can mutate skill instructions through another local tool, and do not rely on the documented calibration/atomic-write safeguards until the implementation actually provides them.
llm.findings:
[TP2] expected: Downgraded: the inspected skill name is ASCII, and the non-ASCII content is visible Chinese description/trigger text rather than a spoofed tool identifier.
[TP4] unexpected: Accepted in substance: several advertised evaluation and safety features are not implemented in the inspected code, which is material because the skill is meant to produce runnable evaluation suites.
[AE1] expected: Downgraded: the cited SKILL.md/task_suite.yaml paths are generated output artifacts, not hidden bundled files that must already exist for review.
[SDI-1] expected: Partly accepted: --auto-improve is documented in the body and README, but the frontmatter also says this skill is not for driving the improvement loop, creating a real scope inconsistency.
[LP3] expected: File read/write and shell-oriented CLI use are expected for this generator, but the skill lacks explicit least-privilege metadata or path-scope guidance.
[SQP-3] unexpected: Partly accepted: free-form purpose words are used to derive triggers, which can produce broad generated-skill activation phrases without review controls.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Partly accepted: triggers such as generate skill and generate task suite are broad for a file-writing tool, though they are visible in the manifest.
[AST4] expected: Downgraded: subprocess use is tied to explicit --evaluate/--auto-improve flags and uses argument lists with shell=False behavior; no command-injection path was found from shell expansion.
[SDI-2] expected: Partly accepted: launching improvement-orchestrator is user-selected and documented, but it expands the generator into orchestration despite contradictory scope language.
[SQP-2] expected: Downgraded: generated file creation is disclosed in SKILL.md and README even though the module docstring itself is less explicit.
[T01] expected: Accepted as a material concern: generating agent instructions from specs is core behavior, but critical_constraints is underdocumented and rendered as authoritative instruction text.
[T09] expected: Accepted as an integrity concern: file output is expected, but the code uses direct truncating writes while documentation claims atomic write-then-rename.
